scenario.prompt_to_agent:
After a "rollback" on r13, R11 reports it lost an EIGRP
neighbor and 113.1.x.x routes disappeared from R11's topology
table. R13 reports EIGRP is running and its config looks valid.
What changed?

injection.action: change EIGRP AS from 100 to 300 (a value R11 doesn't speak)

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r13 EIGRP AS number
Mechanism: EIGRP requires both ends of an adjacency to share
  the same AS. R11 runs AS 100 (covering both R12 and R13
  sides per the collapsed-single-AS fix from earlier). R13
  was reconfigured to AS 300. Hello packets carry the AS,
  the mismatch is detected, and the adjacency never forms.
  R11 stops seeing 113.1.x routes, and R13 stops seeing
  102.x / 112.x / 120.x routes from R12 via R11.
Localization: r13
Root cause: EIGRP AS mismatch (R13 in AS 300, R11/R12 in AS 100)
Fix: re-configure r13 to AS 100
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: EIGRP AS number / EIGRP autonomous system

agent.diagnosis_text: Affected component: FRR EIGRP process/AS on r13. Mechanism: EIGRP only forms adjacencies between routers in the same autonomous system (AS). When the AS numbers don’t match, neighbors do not come up and previously learned routes time out and are withdrawn. Localization: The broken adjacency is on the FF segment between r11.eth2 (103.1.1.1/8) and r13.eth0 (103.1.1.2/8). On r11, “show ip eigrp neighbors” shows a single neighbor 112.1.1.2 on eth0 (r12) and zero peers on eth2, while “show ip eigrp interfaces” confirms no peers on eth2. On r13, “show run” and “show ip eigrp neighbors” show EIGRP running in AS 300 with no neighbors. By contrast, r11’s EIGRP is configured for AS 100 (networks 112.0.0.0/8 and 103.0.0.0/8). Root cause: The rollback on r13 changed its EIGRP autonomous system from 100 to 300, creating an AS mismatch with r11 and causing loss of the 113.1.x.x routes previously learned from r13. Corrective fix: Revert r13 to EIGRP AS 100 (no router eigrp 300; router eigrp 100; network 103.0.0.0/8 and 113.1.0.0/16 or the specific /24s). After aligning the AS, the EIGRP neighbor on r11.eth2 should re-establish with r13.eth0 and the 113.1.x.x routes will repopulate r11’s EIGRP topology and routing tables.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies r13 as the affected device (multiple references to r13 and its EIGRP AS misconfiguration).

per_axis.rationale: The submission explicitly identifies the EIGRP autonomous system on r13 (AS 300) mismatching r11/r12 (AS 100) and pinpoints the FRR EIGRP process/AS as the affected component.
The report clearly explains that an EIGRP AS number mismatch (r13 AS300 vs r11 AS100) prevents adjacencies from forming and provides evidence and the corrective action.
Correctly instructs to reconfigure r13 to EIGRP AS 100 with the appropriate network statements, which will restore the neighbor adjacency and routes.

The logs show r11 running EIGRP AS 100 and r13 running EIGRP AS 300, r11 has a neighbor only on eth0 (112.1.1.2) while r13 shows EIGRP AS(300) with no neighbors — direct evidence that an AS mismatch prevents the adjacency. (Minor note: r11 still has a learned route to 113.1.1.0 via 103.1.1.2 in the routing table, but that does not invalidate the observed AS mismatch.)
